nodes.title: Canonical distance of a process

nodes.summary: In an admissible sequence of partitions, $\operatorname{card} \mathcal{A}_0 \le N_0 = 1$ forces $\mathcal{A}_0 = \{T\}$: every cell $A_0(t)$ is the whole space. In particular the term $n = 0$ of $\sum_n 2^{n/2}\Delta(A_n(t))$ is the diameter $\Delta(T)$, which is why $\Delta(T) \le \gamma_2(T, d)$.

They satisfy $N_n^2 \le N_{n+1}$, and $\sqrt{\log N_n}$ is of order $2^{n/2}$, which is where the weights $2^{n/2}$ of $\gamma_2$ come from: a union bound over $N_n$ sub-Gaussian variables costs a factor $\sqrt{\log N_n}$.

nodes.summary: If the metric of $T$ is $d(s, t) = (\mathbb{E}(X_s - X_t)^2)^{1/2}$ for all $s, t$, then the extended distance of $T$ equals the canonical distance of the process, so $\gamma_2$ computed for the metric and for the canonical distance agree. This links the proved Gaussian bound, stated with the metric, to the majorizing measure theorem, stated with the canonical distance.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.
